memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over Egypt so that locusts swarm over the land and devour everything growing in the fields, everything left by the hail." So Moses stretched out his staff over Egypt, and the Lord made an east wind blow across the land all that day and all that night. By morning the wind had brought the locusts;" - Exodus 10:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice how God brings the locusts. Not by a sudden supernatural appearance, but by an east wind that blows all day and all night.

God uses ordinary means. The wind was real wind. Anyone in Egypt could have felt it on their face. And yet it was entirely God's doing, arriving at exactly the announced time.

We tend to look for God in the spectacular and miss Him in the ordinary. But a change in the weather, a phone call, a delayed train, a person who happens to be in the right place — these are the instruments God most often uses. Providence usually wears everyday clothes.

Notice also the patience of it. All that day and all that night. God's answer was on the way for many hours before anyone saw a single locust.

That is often true of our situations too. What arrives in the morning has been travelling since yesterday.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might God be working through ordinary means that I have overlooked?
2. Can I trust that God's answer may already be on the way, unseen?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to see Your hand in ordinary things. Give me patience while Your answers are still on the way. Amen.
